tasks.title: Scaffold Phase 1 workspace packages
tasks.context: Create the minimal installable package skeletons for Phase 1 only: `packages/core` and `packages/schemas`. The root `pyproject.toml` already declares `[tool.uv.workspace] members = ["packages/*"]`; preserve existing ruff, mypy strict, and pytest settings while adding only what is required for these two packages to install and import. This task must not implement schemas, protocols, matching, scoring, ATS, parsing, export, CLI, MCP, API, persistence, or frontend behavior.
acceptance_criteria: `packages/core` and `packages/schemas` exist as installable src-layout Python packages for Python 3.12+ with `py.typed` markers.
Package import names are stable: `resume_kit_core` and `resume_kit_schemas`.
Root workspace config still includes `packages/*`; no Phase 2+ package directories are created.
Each package has a minimal `pyproject.toml`, `README.md`, `src/.../__init__.py`, and package-local `tests/` directory.
`uv run python -c "import resume_kit_core, resume_kit_schemas"` succeeds after install/sync.
No `app.*` upstream imports are introduced anywhere under `packages/`.
tasks.implementation_notes: Use Hatchling to match the root build backend. Keep skeleton files intentionally minimal so downstream package agents own implementation. Suggested dependency shape: `packages/schemas` depends on `pydantic>=2`; `packages/core` depends on `pydantic>=2` and the workspace `resume-kit-schemas` package if needed. Do not copy code from `./upstream/` in this task. If a lockfile is generated by `uv`, include it in this task's changes.
verification_steps: uv run ruff check pyproject.toml packages/core packages/schemas

tasks.title: Implement canonical schemas and upstream schema characterization
tasks.context: Implement the Phase 1 `schemas` package. It must define canonical Pydantic v2 domain models separated from transport/HTTP DTOs, while porting/adapting only the upstream schema material classified Extract in Phase 0. The upstream file `upstream/apps/backend/app/schemas/models.py` mixes reusable domain models with web/API DTOs; split it so `resume_kit_schemas` contains domain contracts only.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical documented Pydantic v2 models exist for `ResumeDocument`, `JobDescription`, `CandidateEvidence`, `AnalysisReport`, `ChangeProposal`, diff/change-set models, `ClaimProvenance`, warning models, artifact metadata, and generic interface payload primitives needed by Phase 1.

Ported/adapted schema behavior is protected by characterization tests for upstream validation/coercion behavior: description string/list coercion, `descriptionStyles` alignment, optional text coercion, `ResumeData`/`ResumeDocument` default filling, `ResumeChange`/`ChangeProposal` list-original validation, and refinement schema bounds/defaults.

HTTP/web/application DTOs from upstream are explicitly excluded: do not port `ResumeUploadResponse`, `ResumeFetchResponse`, `ResumeListResponse`, `JobUploadRequest`, `JobUploadResponse`, config/API-key DTOs, health/status DTOs, application tracker DTOs, interview-prep DTOs, router persistence DTOs, or frontend-specific response wrappers.
Package exports in `resume_kit_schemas.__init__` expose the public canonical model surface and do not expose upstream `app.*` names as the primary API.

Every upstream-derived or adapted schema source/test file includes the attribution comment block required by `references/attribution.md`, with upstream path and pinned SHA `116f9cc3b00e1ac91734a6c2679bf41ea64a0edc`.
`references/attribution.md` is updated with the concrete new `packages/schemas` files that port or adapt schema material.
No scoring, matching, ATS algorithms, parsing, alignment application, export, storage, CLI, MCP, API, persistence, frontend, network, or LLM behavior is implemented.
tasks.implementation_notes: Primary upstream sources to review and port/adapt from: `upstream/apps/backend/app/schemas/models.py:140-923` for `PersonalInfo`, `Experience`, `Education`, `Project`, `AdditionalInfo`, `CustomSection`, `ResumeData`, `ResumeChange`, `ResumeFieldDiff`, `ResumeDiffSummary`, and `ImproveDiffResult`; `upstream/apps/backend/app/schemas/refinement.py` for `KeywordGapAnalysis`, `AlignmentViolation`, `AlignmentReport`, `RefinementConfig`, `RefinementStats`, and `RefinementResult` as schema-only primitives. Useful upstream tests to adapt as characterization tests: `upstream/apps/backend/tests/unit/test_description_styles.py`, schema-related assertions in `upstream/apps/backend/tests/unit/test_verify_diffs.py`, `upstream/apps/backend/tests/unit/test_improve_confirm_hash.py` for canonical round-trip behavior, and `upstream/apps/backend/tests/evals/test_scorers.py::TestIsValidResume` for validation expectations. Prefer modules such as `resume.py`, `job.py`, `evidence.py`, `changes.py`, `analysis.py`, and `artifacts.py` under `resume_kit_schemas`; keep names canonical even when behavior is adapted from upstream.
verification_steps: uv run ruff check packages/schemas references/attribution.md
uv run python -c "from resume_kit_schemas import ResumeDocument, JobDescription, CandidateEvidence, AnalysisReport, ChangeProposal"
rg "from app|import app" packages/schemas && exit 1 || true

tasks.title: Implement core provider, response, and artifact contracts
tasks.context: Implement the Phase 1 `core` package as dependency-inversion contracts only. This package defines provider/storage Protocol boundaries and shared response/error abstractions used by later phases, but it must not implement concrete LiteLLM, parsing, matching, scoring, ATS, alignment, export, persistence, CLI, MCP, API, or frontend behavior.
acceptance_criteria: `StructuredCompletionProvider` is a `Protocol` with async `complete_json(request: StructuredCompletionRequest) -> dict[str, Any]` or an equivalently typed JSON-object result.
An LLM-agnostic completion boundary exists with typed request metadata, provider/model options, deterministic test hooks, timeout/retry metadata as data only, and no concrete provider imports.
Artifact/storage Protocols exist for writing/reading generated artifacts or artifact references without persistence implementation details leaking into core.

A generic `InterfaceResponse[T]` envelope exists with `data`, `warnings`, `errors`, `requires_human_input`, `questions`, `artifacts`, and `provenance` fields; it is typed, documented, serializable, and usable with schema payloads.
Core warning/error/provenance/question/artifact value types are Pydantic v2 models or typed dataclasses with strict mypy-compatible annotations.
A fake in-memory structured completion provider exists under `resume_kit_core.testing` or package-local tests and is used by contract tests; tests make no network or LLM calls.
`resume_kit_core.__init__` exports the public Protocols and value types.
No concrete LiteLLM, provider SDK, database, filesystem persistence, parser, matching, scoring, ATS, alignment, export, CLI, MCP, API, frontend, or upstream `app.*` import is introduced.
tasks.implementation_notes: Use `typing.Protocol`, `TypeVar`, `Generic`, `Mapping`, and explicit Pydantic v2 models where they improve validation. Keep provider outputs JSON-compatible and deterministic. The upstream direction to invert is from `upstream/apps/backend/app/llm.py` and services that call `app.llm.complete_json`, but do not port `llm.py` in Phase 1; only define the contract that Phase 2+ adapters will implement. Core may depend on `resume_kit_schemas` for shared schema payload/provenance/artifact model types if the scaffold has declared that dependency, but avoid requiring schema implementation details in provider contracts so this task can be worked in parallel with schemas.
verification_steps: uv run python -c "from resume_kit_core import StructuredCompletionProvider, StructuredCompletionRequest, InterfaceResponse"
rg "litellm|from app|import app|sqlalchemy|fastapi|click|typer" packages/core && exit 1 || true

tasks.title: Add Phase 1 boundary and integration quality gates
tasks.context: Add repo-level tests that prove Phase 1 delivered only the clean core and canonical schema foundation. This task should validate package integration and architectural boundaries without taking ownership of implementation files in `packages/core` or `packages/schemas`. If failures expose package bugs, route fixes back to the owning package task rather than patching those package files here.
acceptance_criteria: A repo-level boundary test asserts only `packages/core` and `packages/schemas` exist under `packages/` for Phase 1.
A repo-level import test imports the public `resume_kit_core` and `resume_kit_schemas` surfaces together, including `InterfaceResponse` parameterized or instantiated with a schema payload.

A boundary test scans `packages/` and fails on upstream `app.*` imports, concrete provider imports such as `litellm`, web/API imports such as `fastapi`, persistence imports such as `sqlalchemy`, and Phase 2+ package names or directories.
A workspace/package metadata test confirms both packages are uv workspace members through the root `packages/*` pattern and have `py.typed` markers.
Full local quality commands are documented and pass: ruff, strict mypy for both packages, and pytest for package and repo-level tests.
No implementation behavior is added for matching, scoring, ATS, alignment, parsing, export, persistence, CLI, MCP, API, or frontend.
tasks.implementation_notes: Place tests under root `tests/`, for example `tests/test_phase1_boundaries.py` and `tests/test_phase1_imports.py`. Use standard library file scanning/TOML parsing available in Python 3.12 (`tomllib`) rather than adding new dependencies. Keep these tests deterministic and network-free. Do not edit `packages/core/`, `packages/schemas/`, or `references/attribution.md` in this task.
verification_steps: uv run ruff check packages tests
uv run pytest packages/core packages/schemas tests
rg "from app|import app" packages && exit 1 || true
